name: protocol-adapter
instruction: Review the target file for provider or transport mechanics leaking past their adapter, or copied agent policy inside adapters. Read root AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, the relevant Agent model-connection implementation, and its callers. OpenAI Responses, Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, ACP, MCP, and the city bridge have real differences. Those differences should be translated where their protocols meet the shared session/tool interface. Report shared city, permission, turn, recording, or planning behavior forked by protocol, or protocol payload/streaming details that force unrelated callers to branch, when you can trace the duplicate policy or leak. Identify the existing seam and the specific knowledge crossing it. Before asserting ACP compliance, establish the protocol/SDK version actually used by the repo and inspect the relevant pinned SDK source or matching official specification evidence. State the concrete obligation and its evidence; if unavailable, report no protocol-compliance finding rather than inventing an obligation from memory. Provider-required headers, stream event mapping, authentication, cancellation, error interpretation, response formats, and protocol capability constraints can legitimately remain distinct adapters. Do not merge them into a misleading universal payload, erase supported protocol behavior, or demand a speculative adapter for a format the product does not support. The external mayor owns its own process/sign-in and need not expose built-in model internals. Its city-only prompt is guidance, not host enforcement over the external agent's own tools: report injected agent-specific permissions or external tool-name filters that mistake that prompt for a permission mechanism. Anchor findings to the target lines and give the observed caller consequence. Report no finding for necessary translation or merely different SDK shapes.
